keys.name: INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL
keys.reason: the in-network address of the api service. Never operator-settable: pointing the frontend at anything but http://api:8080 within this topology is a misconfiguration, not a choice.

keys.name: PUBLIC_ORIGIN
keys.reason: fed from the operator key VIZRA_PUBLIC_ORIGIN; see env/registry/aliases.json.

keys.name: PORT
keys.reason: the in-container port; the published port is VIZRA_FRONTEND_PORT.

keys.name: HOSTNAME
keys.reason: binds inside the container so caddy can reach it over the compose network. No port is published by the base file, so this is not an exposure.

escape_hatch_note: vizra-user declares none. Its test-harness variables (E2E_*, CI, TEST_WORKER_INDEX) are not service configuration and are deliberately absent from this snapshot and from every template.
drift_ignore_note: Baked into the image by vizra-user's Dockerfile and never varied per deployment: NODE_ENV=production is what makes it a production build at all, and NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 is a build-time opt-out. Neither is service configuration, so neither belongs in an operator template.
commands_note: vizra-user ships no operator CLI; its image CMD is `node server.js`.
source_commit_rule: Names a commit on vizra-user's `main`, NOT on a branch. The previous value 77305009 was the tip of an unmerged PR branch: a snapshot stamped with a commit that may never merge cannot be re-derived by anyone, and the drift check would compare against a tree that does not exist for them. Verified at re-stamp time by reading lib/config.ts and Dockerfile out of `git show origin/main:` - the three keys and the two image ENV declarations are unchanged. The same rule applies to every registry here.
